paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of Rav Yehudah, in Avodah Zarah 26a: Rav Menashe was traveling to Bei Toreta when thieves met him. They said to him, "Where are you going?" He said to them, "To Pumbedita." When he reached Bei Toreta he separated from them. They said to him, "Are you a student of Yehudah, a deceiver?" He said to them, "Do you know him? May you be under his ban."
And thus we find him together with Rabbah and Rav Yosef, in Eruvin 104a: Ulla happened to come to the house of Rav Menashe; a certain man came and knocked at the door — Rabbah replied to him, etc.
And in Shabbat 156a: Rav Menashe said [Hyman says it should read so, as in Chullin 4a, Tosafot s.v. Makhnim] "one before another" — Rav Yosef said, "even," etc.
He is mentioned in Yevamot 25b: he said that a robber by rabbinic law is fit to testify for a woman.

And in Chullin we have three halakhic statements from him (the mnemonic: makhnisin, izmel, zekharim). There, 4a, he explains it as referring to bringing them beneath his cloak; and there, 31a, he said regarding a scalpel without protrusions [literally, horns]; Rav Acha son of Rav Avya (Hyman says it should read Rav Avya, for Rav Acha bar Avya was in the time of Rav Ashi) said to Rav Menashe, "A needle, what is it?" etc. And there, 51a, he said: these rams stolen by thieves, we do not worry about crushing of limbs.

And in Shabbat 74b, Rav Menashe said: one who cuts wood into splinters is liable for grinding; and he is mentioned there after Rav Pappa. Hyman finds the reading of Dikdukei Soferim, "Rav Ashi said," easier, and reports that this is also the Soncino reading.

notes.text: The named Davidson Avodah Zarah26a has Do you know him? followed by a ban; Eruvin104a makes Rabbah the respondent, not a vocative. Shabbat74b places Rav Pappa before Rav Menashe: ר״פ is not beginning of chapter.
The knife/mnemonic passages and the precise wood-splinter gloss still require their full commentary context. Hyman’s Acha/Avya correction and Soncino/Dikdukei Soferim reading remain his reports.

The whole printed notice spans volume III, pp. 894–895. The whole consulted Tosafot on Chullin 4a, beginning מכניס איזמל בזכרים, names Rav Menashe and explains the three-part mnemonic through the cloak, scalpel and stolen-rams passages; it also cites the ‘one before another’ saying in Shabbat 156. This supports the local mnemonic context, without proving that every namesake notice is one person. The whole Rashi on Shabbat 74b gloss explains the wood as small pieces for kindling; the local Gemara places Rav Pappa before Rav Menashe, rather than referring to the beginning of a chapter. Hyman’s preferred Rav Ashi reading and report about Soncino remain attributed to him: those exact apparatus and printed witnesses have not been collated. The whole Chullin 31a dialogue retains Rav Acha son of Rav Avya asking Rav Menashe about a needle, beside Hyman’s definite proposed replacement with Rav Avya on chronological grounds. The source is not silently repaired. The whole Chullin 51a paragraph has Rav Menashei’s stolen-rams saying and further qualifications not inserted into Hyman’s abridgment. Avodah Zarah’s whole 25b ending continues into 26a with the thieves, ‘Do you know him?’ and the ban; Eruvin’s next whole paragraph makes Rabbah the respondent. Hyman’s student/chronology claims remain his; the supplied מכנים and אויא/עויא forms are not normalized. All Hebrew and current notes remain unchanged.
